texts.NIV84: An unfriendly man pursues selfish ends; he defies all sound judgment.
texts.KJV: Through desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh and intermeddleth with all wisdom.
texts.NKJV:
A man who isolates himself seeks his own desire;
He rages against all wise judgment.
texts.DRB: He that hath a mind to depart from a friend seeketh occasions: he shall ever be subject to reproach.

texts.NIV84: A fool finds no pleasure in understanding but delights in airing his own opinions.
texts.KJV: A fool hath no delight in understanding, but that his heart may discover itself.
texts.NKJV:
A fool has no delight in understanding,
But in expressing his own heart.
texts.DRB: A fool receiveth not the words of prudence: unless thou say those things which are in his heart.

texts.NIV84: When wickedness comes, so does contempt, and with shame comes disgrace.
texts.KJV: When the wicked cometh, then cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.
texts.NKJV:
When the wicked comes, contempt comes also;
And with dishonor comes reproach.
texts.DRB: The wicked man when he is come into the depth of sins, contemneth: but ignominy and reproach follow him.

texts.NIV84: The words of a man's mouth are deep waters, but the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.
texts.KJV: The words of a man's mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook.
texts.NKJV:
The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters;
The wellspring of wisdom is a flowing brook.
texts.DRB: Words from the mouth of a men are as deep water: and the fountain of wisdom as an overflowing stream.

texts.NIV84: It is not good to be partial to the wicked or to deprive the innocent of justice.
texts.KJV: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to overthrow the righteous in judgment.
texts.NKJV:
It is not good to show partiality to the wicked,
Or to overthrow the righteous in judgment.
texts.DRB: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to decline from the truth of judgment.

blocks.title: The Lips and Mouth of a Fool

texts.NIV84: A fool's lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.
texts.KJV: A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.
texts.NKJV:
A fool’s lips enter into contention,
And his mouth calls for blows.
texts.DRB: The lips of a fool intermeddle with strife: and his mouth provoketh quarrels.

texts.NIV84: A fool's mouth is his undoing, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
texts.KJV: A fool's mouth is his destruction, and his lips are the snare of his soul.
texts.NKJV:
A fool’s mouth is his destruction,
And his lips are the snare of his soul.
texts.DRB: The mouth of a fool is his destruction: and his lips are the ruin of his soul.

texts.NIV84: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down to a man's inmost parts.
texts.KJV: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
texts.NKJV:
The words of a talebearer are like tasty trifles,
And they go down into the inmost body.
texts.DRB: The words of the double tongued are as if they were harmless: and they reach even to the inner parts of the bowels. Fear casteth down the slothful: and the souls of the effeminate shall be hungry.

texts.NIV84: One who is slack in his work is brother to one who destroys.
texts.KJV: He also that is slothful in his work is brother to him that is a great waster.
texts.NKJV:
He who is slothful in his work
Is a brother to him who is a great destroyer.
texts.DRB: He that is loose and slack in his work, is the brother of him that wasteth his own works.

texts.NIV84: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
texts.KJV: The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
texts.NKJV:
The name of the Lord is a strong tower;
The righteous run to it and are safe.
texts.DRB: The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the just runneth to it, and shall be exalted.

texts.NIV84: The wealth of the rich is their fortified city; they imagine it an unscalable wall.
texts.KJV: The rich man's wealth is his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.
texts.NKJV:
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city,
And like a high wall in his own esteem.
texts.DRB: The substance of the rich man is the city of his strength, and as a strong wall compassing him about.

texts.NIV84: Before his downfall a man's heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
texts.KJV: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility.
texts.NKJV:
Before destruction the heart of a man is haughty,
And before honor is humility.
texts.DRB: Before destruction, the heart of a man is exalted: and before he be glorified, it is humbled.

texts.NIV84: He who answers before listening- that is his folly and his shame.
texts.KJV: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
texts.NKJV:
He who answers a matter before he hears it,
It is folly and shame to him.
texts.DRB: He that answereth before he heareth sheweth himself to be a fool, and worthy of confusion.

texts.NIV84: A man's spirit sustains him in sickness, but a crushed spirit who can bear?
texts.KJV: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?
texts.NKJV:
The spirit of a man will sustain him in sickness,
But who can bear a broken spirit?
texts.DRB: The spirit of a man upholdeth his infirmity: but a spirit that is easily angered, who can bear?

texts.NIV84: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge; the ears of the wise seek it out.
texts.KJV: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
texts.NKJV:
The heart of the prudent acquires knowledge,
And the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
texts.DRB: A wise heart shall acquire knowledge: and the ear of the wise seeketh instruction.

texts.NIV84: A gift opens the way for the giver and ushers him into the presence of the great.
texts.KJV: A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
texts.NKJV:
A man’s gift makes room for him,
And brings him before great men.
texts.DRB: A man's gift enlargeth his may, and maketh him room before princes.

texts.NIV84: The first to present his case seems right, till another comes forward and questions him.
texts.KJV: He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
texts.NKJV:
The first one to plead his cause seems right,
Until his neighbor comes and examines him.
texts.DRB: The just is first accuser of himself: his friend cometh, and shall search him.

texts.NIV84: Casting the lot settles disputes and keeps strong opponents apart.
texts.KJV: The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.
texts.NKJV:
Casting lots causes contentions to cease,
And keeps the mighty apart.
texts.DRB: The lot suppresseth contentions, and determineth even between the mighty.

texts.NIV84: An offended brother is more unyielding than a fortified city, and disputes are like the barred gates of a citadel.
texts.KJV: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.
texts.NKJV:
A brother offended is harder to win than a strong city,
And contentions are like the bars of a castle.
texts.DRB: A brother that is helped by his brother, is like a strong city: and judgments are like the bars of cities.

blocks.title: Death and Life in the Tongue

texts.NIV84: From the fruit of his mouth a man's stomach is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
texts.KJV: A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; and with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.
texts.NKJV:
A man’s stomach shall be satisfied from the fruit of his mouth;
From the produce of his lips he shall be filled.
texts.DRB: Of the fruit of a man's mouth shall his belly be satisfied: and the offspring of his lips shall fill him.

texts.NIV84: The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
texts.KJV: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
texts.NKJV:
Death and life are in the power of the tongue,
And those who love it will eat its fruit.
texts.DRB: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: they that love it, shall eat the fruits thereof.

texts.NIV84: He who finds a wife finds what is good and receives favor from the LORD.
texts.KJV: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the Lord.
texts.NKJV:
He who finds a wife finds a good thing,
And obtains favor from the Lord.
texts.DRB: He that hath found a good wife, hath found a good thing, and shall receive a pleasure from the Lord. He that driveth away a good wife, driveth away a good thing: but he that keepeth an adulteress, is foolish and wicked.

texts.NIV84: A poor man pleads for mercy, but a rich man answers harshly.
texts.KJV: The poor useth intreaties; but the rich answereth roughly.
texts.NKJV:
The poor man uses entreaties,
But the rich answers roughly.
texts.DRB: The poor will speak with supplications, and the rich will speak roughly.

texts.NIV84: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
texts.KJV: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
texts.NKJV:
A man who has friends must himself be friendly,
But there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
texts.DRB: A man amiable in society, shall be more friendly than a brother.
